texts.value: G protein-coupled receptor for CRH, UCN, UCN2 and UCN3 stress hormones, which plays a central role in whole body adaptation to stress (PubMed:11329063, PubMed:11416224, PubMed:20966082, PubMed:22689579, PubMed:32004470, PubMed:36335102). Has highest affinity for UCN, and much lower affinity for CRH, UNC2 and UCN3 (PubMed:20966082, PubMed:22689579, PubMed:32004470, PubMed:36335102). Ligand binding causes a conformation change that triggers signaling via guanine nucleotide-binding proteins (G proteins) and downstream effectors, such as adenylate cyclase (PubMed:32004470, PubMed:36335102). CRHR2 is coupled to G(s) G protein (GNAS), mediating activation of adenylate cyclase activity and production of cAMP (PubMed:32004470, PubMed:36335102). CRHR2-dependent signaling is a primary mediator of the neuroendocrine, autonomic (fight-or-flight) and behavioral responses to stress, acting as a key regulator of adaptation by activating the hypothalamus-pituitary-adrenal axis, leading to corticotropin hormone (ACTH) production (By similarity)

The uncleaved pseudo signal peptide prevents receptor's oligomerization and coupling to G(i) subunits (PubMed:22689579). It is also responsible for the rather low receptor localization at the plasma membrane (PubMed:22689579)
A N-glycosylation site within the signal peptide impedes its proper cleavage and function
Belongs to the G protein-coupled receptor 2 family
